messages:
maya: quick heads-up — ran AWQ + per-layer clamp prototype on model-psi-3B this morning, got weird high-tail channels on mid transformer blocks, specifically layer_6 and layer_17.
Sanjay: ugh. delta PPL +3.2 on the longform-summ eval or just a few QA items?
maya: longform-summ got the +3.2, MMLU unchanged. QA-bench precision dropped on some named-entity pairs (precision -4 pts).
linh: did you check KV-cache friendliness? sometimes AWQ packing screws up KV scale in mid layers.
maya: KV looks ok. The problematic channels show 10-100x activation spikes vs baseline for some prompts. Attached quick CLI dump: 
```
python infra/scan_outliers.py --model model-psi-3B --quant awq --per-layer --topk 50 --out /tmp/psi-outliers.csv
```
kevin: can you paste the top offending channels snippet? 
maya: pasted small table below (layer,channel,max/mean): layer_6,c24,48.2; layer_6,c61,37.9; layer_17,c3,92.1; layer_17,c44,41.5
Sanjay: interesting — those channels line up with sparse attention heads? Could be firmware/kernel numerical edge.
eva: suggestion: try surgical skip for those channels (force fp16 for channel region) and re-run quant. We did similar on psi-2 and it recovered ~+2 PPL.
linh: alternative: channel-wise clamp before quantization with scale=median(abs)/0.5 heuristic, or hybrid: AWQ everywhere + GPTQ fallback for layers 6 and 17.
kevin: ops-bot, can you spin a dedicated run with: AWQ global, but layers [6,17] as int8-gptq fallback, and report evals?
ops-bot: deploying job job-19955 on dedicated-runner-7: config {"quant_profile":"awq+layer-fallback","fallback_layers":[6,17],"evals":["longform-summ","qa-bench","mmlu"]}. ETA ~3h. :gear:
maya: thanks. parallel note — also try a tiny experiment: keep AWQ but apply per-channel clamp factor of 0.8 only for the offending channels, not whole layer, to see perf vs accuracy tradeoff.
Sanjay: good call. We should capture per-token latency delta and tokens/sec difference — fallback layers may add 12–18% latency but might be worth accuracy.
eva: also add a quick regression harness: run those same prompts with FP8 baseline, AWQ raw, AWQ+clamp, AWQ+fallback. Keep seed & prompt set identical.
kevin: if fallback wins, we can add a routing policy in the serving runtime: route problematic traffic to fallback-model-psi-3B-gptq for short contexts. Might be simpler than full model re-quant.
linh: logging suggestion: record per-request flagged_channels list so we can correlate output errors with activation spikes.
maya: agreed. I'll collate the failing prompts and push to the eval dashboard once ops-bot finishes.
Sanjay: final ask — add a small script to auto-detect channels with max/mean > 12x baseline and suggest either clamp OR channel-gate list for surgical-quant step. Could save manual triage.
maya: noted — I'll prototype the detector this afternoon and tag you. Short follow-up once job completes. :thumbsup:
